Chapter Details: Status of national population, civil, address, land, business, electoral, tax and social protection registers. 44 variables in 8 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Does the government maintain a digital population register?
Comments: No clear evidence of a distinct, standalone national population register; Fayda foundational digital ID (Proc. 1284/2023) collects core demographic attributes and targets covering all residents, which can function as a de facto population register backbone.
revision_notes: Original score of 2 (Planned) understated the current status. Ethiopia has no standalone population register, but the Fayda digital ID (est. under Proclamation 1284/2023) is confirmed live and actively enrolling residents nationwide, not merely planned: id.gov.et shows an operating registration platform; Biometric Update (June 2025) reported 16.4 million enrolled with a roadmap to 90 million by 2027; CGTN (2 July 2026) reports over 46 million registered (roughly a third of the ~126 million population) with nearly 165 institutions integrated into the national database. This is active, large-scale rollout, not full nationwide coverage, so recalculated to 4 = Partially deployed against the reg-pop-exists scale (0=Unknown; 1=No; 2=Planned; 3=Under development; 4=Partially deployed; 5=Fully deployed nationwide). Original World Bank source (2024) confirms Fayda's design intent to cover all residents but does not itself establish deployment scale, superseded here by more current enrolment figures.
revised_comments: Ethiopia does not maintain a distinct, standalone national population register. Instead, the Fayda foundational digital identity system, established under the Digital Identification Proclamation No. 1284/2023 and administered by the National ID Program, functions as the country's de facto population register, capturing core demographic data (full name, date of birth, gender, address, citizenship) and biometrics (fingerprints, iris, facial image) for residents on a one-person-one-identity basis. Registration is live and expanding nationwide: as of July 2026 more than 46 million people have enrolled, equivalent to roughly a third of Ethiopia's population of around 126 million, with nearly 165 institutions including banks, digital payment providers and public agencies integrated with the national database. The programme's stated target is to enrol upwards of 90 million residents by 2027, indicating the register is partially, but not yet fully, deployed nationwide.
